timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream only; semantic events are projected through the raw serial agent log.
Serial trajectory explores, writes the project, iterates build fixes, runs differential tests, adds unit tests, verifies final builds, and reports completion.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the prompt obligations: pure Rust 2021, std only, exact atoi-like CLI, trailing-space byte output, a complete /output Cargo project, and black-box validation against the reference binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first launched a broad reconstruction workflow, but also kept implementation ownership itself and independently built the final /output artifact. A second workflow owned adversarial verification after the artifact existed.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented an arena-index earcut port under /output with Rust modules for atoi, shape, earcut core, holes, predicates, z-order, and the test19.rs entry. It corrected build issues and produced both rustc and cargo binaries.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final deliverable was parent-authored and placed in /output before the wait period; child build candidates from the first workflow never reached a stage that overwrote or integrated into /output.
parallel.verification: The parent validated with 131 ground-truth cases, exhaustive -20..700 and larger n sweeps, CLI edge cases, cargo build, cargo test, and timing comparisons. The later verifier workflow found additional edge issues but did not return an aggregate result before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The artifact passed the official evaluator, but the parent timed out with an empty final response while both workflows were killed; the verifier workflow had unreturned findings about non-UTF-8 CLI handling and hole-path behavior.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same pure Rust, exact CLI/output, zero dependency, Cargo project, test19.rs, and black-box requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With workflow tools disabled, the serial parent owned exploration, implementation, integration, verification, and final reporting end to end.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote a modular Rust project under /output with cli, fractal, and earcut modules plus test19.rs, iterating the implementation until the reference outputs matched.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was assembled directly in /output with Cargo.toml, test19.rs, compiled test19 executable, and supporting modules; no child artifacts required reconciliation.
serial.verification: The serial run used broad byte-exact differential testing, CLI edge checks, cargo and rustc builds, debug checks, unit tests, and runtime comparison before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process completed normally with a final report and official pass. No delegated work or trapped child result remained.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel explicitly pursued byte-exact Rust output, std-only implementation, cargo/rustc buildability, and /output placement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial pursued the same prompt obligations and documented them in its final verification summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement interpretation difference affected the official outcome; the difference was later closure after parallel delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split recall/spec/build and verification into workflows while the parent still kept and completed the final implementation itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflow tools disabled and kept all stages in one parent-controlled trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child result lifecycle risk after implementation; serial had no child ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included the task context and strict per-child work directories; the verifier brief described /output and the requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept requirements and current file state local to the parent, avoiding cross-agent interface transfer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Context transfer itself was adequate; the issue arose from return timing of verifier findings, not an incomplete brief or missing interface contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the final implementation directly in /output after validating a /tmp/mine prototype and fixing build imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its own modular implementation in /output and iterated on build/test feedback.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations solved the official single-ring task, but they used different module layouts and different verification side investigations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the verifier workflow after /output passed tests, but the workflow was killed with result null while completed child findings were recorded only in the workflow journal.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification results stayed in the parent trajectory and were incorporated into the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a parent-consumable verifier return; serial closed its verification loop without a child return boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final /output tree was written by the parent; workflow children mostly wrote /tmp or inspected /output, with no proven overwrite of the submitted artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the final /output tree directly and did not have concurrent child writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained shared-state collision was observed; parallel's shared state risk did not materialize into a write conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed broad parent-side byte comparisons and official evaluation passed, while verifier children later reported additional non-official findings that stayed unreturned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed broad differential tests, build checks, and unit tests, then official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had enough verification for official pass; only parallel left additional delegated verification feedback outside the parent decision loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used two workflows, 13 children, and over two million workflow-child tokens before the parent process was killed at the timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no children, completed normally with returncode 0, and still passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's post-artifact workflow wait consumed closure time and left no final response; serial finished and reported normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. Both current completed status evaluations passed 38 of 38 tests. The important difference is that the parallel artifact was complete and accepted before the parent timed out while waiting on workflows, whereas the serial parent completed and returned a final report.
parallel_contributors: Parent-authored /output implementation passed broad local tests before timeout.
Verifier workflow findings remained below a killed workflow and did not change the submitted artifact.
serial_contributors: Single parent owned implementation, verification, and reporting end to end.
Serial final response recorded completed verification and normal closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two implementations used different module layouts and slightly different auxiliary library surfaces, but both satisfied the official single-task evaluator.
evaluator_effects: Official evaluator scope accepted both artifacts despite parallel process timeout and despite verifier findings outside the official tested path.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a process consequence only

candidates.reason: The parent kept implementation ownership and wrote the final /output project itself, so implementation was not unowned.
There were no independently completed component implementations requiring an unowned reconciliation step; parent integrated its own project.
The parent assembled Cargo.toml, modules, test19.rs, and the executable in /output before timeout.
The parent owned the end-to-end implementation, build, testing, and delivery pipeline; the workflow wait was not an owner omission.
Implementation was not blocked behind a serial preflight; the parent built the passing artifact while the reconstruction workflow was still running.
The parallel parent did not defer all productive implementation until investigation completed; it implemented and verified concurrently with child investigation.
The indispensable implementation path was not starved; it completed, was packaged, and passed official evaluation.
The run had broad fan-out and a timeout, but the more specific observed boundary is the verifier result not returning; high child count alone is insufficient.
No single child was shown to own an indispensable overbroad implementation task whose incompletion prevented delivery.
The child briefs included task requirements, environment, acceptance style, and output context; no unusable work is traced to an omitted known requirement.
The delegated work did not produce separately owned components that failed to interoperate because of an omitted file, API, namespace, or output contract.
No known finding or requirement is shown to disappear through transfer and cause repeated work or a wrong action.
Although some child reports were large, no available parent-level handoff was too bulky to reduce; the verifier aggregate never returned.
No receiver is shown consuming a superseded child result or stale workspace description to make a wrong integration decision.
The parent did not receive conflicting handoffs and leave them unadjudicated; relevant verifier findings remained below the killed workflow.
The parent did not make an unsupported completion decision after a visible integrated gap; it had broad tests and then timed out without a final response.
The workflow did retry stalled spec agents, but they received accumulated recall material and no repeated-work consequence displaced the delivered artifact.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The kill was the global run timeout, not an explicit parent or orchestration cancellation of a child before a needed result.
A complete candidate was already promoted, packaged, placed in /output, and officially accepted; finalization did not start too late.
No child implementation change was merged after integrated verification without a post-merge check.
The retained workflow findings were verifier findings, not a completed delegated implementation that the parent failed to adopt.

The verifier workflow delegated hunter agents and two completed with concrete findings, but the workflow itself was killed with result null before those findings returned as a parent-consumable aggregate.
candidates.realized_consequence: Concrete verifier findings about non-UTF-8 CLI handling and hole-path behavior were not returned to or acted on by the parent before the run closed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did not receive a completed aggregate verifier result and ignore it; the findings were trapped below the killed workflow boundary.

candidates.reason: The parent was killed by the run timeout and had already delivered a passing artifact; the direct observed problem is missing verifier return, not takeover of a required failed implementation child.
The concrete verifier findings were not available as a completed parent-level result; they remained in workflow child results while the workflow aggregate was null.
The parent periodically checked workflow progress and artifacts while waiting, so the record is not a wait without inspection.
Workflow children did not produce competing implementation files that claimed the same final behavior and required reconciliation in /output.
No two live actors are shown editing the same submitted source file with one observing or reconciling the other's change.
No actor replaced non-entry source that another live actor actively owned in the submitted tree.
The parent rebuilt /output/test19 as part of its own deliverable workflow; no child or competing actor overwrote the submitted entry artifact.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's completed final-tree work in /output.
Although children used shared temporary and dataset paths, no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem affected the submitted /output artifact.
No generated artifact from one concurrent actor is shown being consumed by another actor as the stable reference environment in a way that contaminated the final solution.
